en.title: Maximum Contiguous Quality Score After Changing Exactly One Range
en.description:
You must choose a non-empty range and either multiply all of it by impactFactor or divide all of it by that factor, rounding toward 0. After the operation, find the maximum possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n impactFactor (1≤n≤200000, 1≤impactFactor≤10000); the second line contains n ratings (−100000..100000).
en.explanation: Example 1: multiplying the last 2 and 4 by 2 turns them into 4 and 8, for a maximum sum of 12. Example 2: a factor of 1 changes nothing, so choosing 3 gives 3. Example 3: −3 divided by 2 rounded toward 0 is −1, which is the maximum quality score obtainable.
hints: Handle multiplication and division separately, using a three-state contiguous subarray DP for not yet in the modified range, currently modifying, and already left it. Take the maximum subarray sum that contains at least one modified position.
